title: Standardize metric labels and reduce cardinality for Private installs
author: Thomas Baird
release_notes: Private: Reduce Prometheus metric cardinality by standardizing labels and bounding route/model dimensions. Backwards-compatible via dual-emission + recording rules for a deprecation window.
body: Context: Private installs run customer-managed Prometheus with tighter TSDB/storage limits and stricter cardinality constraints than our hosted environments. We observed high series churn from per-request and per-route/model labels, especially when customers have many routes, frequently changing model versions, or multi-tenant traffic. This PR standardizes label names across control plane + data plane services and introduces bounded label strategies for Private (while keeping a compatibility path for existing dashboards/alerts). Scope: (1) Label normalization: unify common label keys across services (service/component/namespace/cluster), rename inconsistent keys (route vs endpoint, model vs model_name), and remove labels that should never exist on metrics (request_id, raw path). (2) Cardinality reduction for Private: replace unbounded labels with bounded dimensions: route_group (config-defined, limited set), model_family (derived, bounded), tenant_bucket (optional, hashed bucket count), and status_class (2xx/4xx/5xx). (3) Compatibility: dual-emit old + new metrics/labels for a deprecation window behind a feature flag, plus recording rules that map old queries to new series so dashboards/alerts keep working. (4) Documentation: add guidance in the Private metrics standards doc and inline comments explaining why certain labels are disallowed. Implementation details: - Added a shared metrics helper package used by gateway, policy/routing, and runtime sidecars to enforce label allowlists and cap label values. - Introduced `REDWOOD_PRIVATE_METRICS_MODE=bounded` (default on for Private Helm values; off by default in hosted/dev) to enable bounding behavior. - For route dimension: emit `route_group` (from route config; defaults to "default"; max 50 distinct values per cluster enforced with "other" overflow). - For model dimension: emit `model_family` (e.g., llama3, mistral, qwen; unknown -> "other") and `model_variant` (optional; capped to top-N by request volume per process; overflow -> "other"). - For tenant dimension: do not emit raw tenant_id; emit `tenant_bucket` only when enabled (default disabled) to support coarse multi-tenant skew debugging without exploding series. - Removed `path` label usage from HTTP metrics in gateway; replaced with `route_group` + `handler` (bounded). - Updated recording rules used by the minimum pack dashboards to prefer the new labels, while still supporting legacy selectors. Notes: This is a stepping stone for the Private observability minimum pack (dashboards/alerts). Keeping dual emission avoids a hard cutover, but we should schedule removal once the minimum pack GA branch is stable. Testing: - Unit tests assert label allowlist enforcement and overflow behavior. - Added a micro-benchmark for the label bounding map to ensure we don’t introduce hot-path locks. - Verified in the private smoke-test harness that series count stays within expected limits on a synthetic 200-route / 80-model workload. Rollout plan: - Enable bounded mode by default for Private Helm chart values (separate PR in charts). - Keep legacy labels available for 2 releases; emit a log warning in bounded mode when legacy selectors are detected (dashboard queries) only in debug builds (no customer-facing noise). - Document migration in `docs/private/observability/metrics-migrations.md` and link in alert annotations where relevant.
commits: metrics: add label allowlist + bounded label utilities for private mode
gateway: replace path label with route_group + handler; remove request_id label leak
routing: standardize labels for policy engine metrics (status_class, route_group)
runtime: switch model label emission to model_family/model_variant with top-N cap
telemetry: add recording rules to bridge legacy selectors to bounded labels
docs: add private metrics label standards + migration notes
changed_files: deploy/charts/redwood/values.schema.json (wire env var + defaults for private)
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we ensure we never emit raw tenant identifiers in labels? Even hashed labels can be risky if the hash is stable. Suggest bucketing only and keep default off.
Thomas Baird (author): Agreed. Updated to `tenant_bucket` (configurable bucket count) and default disabled. Removed stable hash emission; tests added to enforce no `tenant_id` label anywhere.

Nadia Rahman (review): Dual emission is good, but please confirm the recording rules don’t re-introduce high cardinality (e.g., by grouping over model_variant). Also want clarity on top-N cap semantics.

Thomas Baird (author): Recording rules group by `model_family` only; `model_variant` is only emitted when enabled and capped. Added doc comment + unit test verifying overflow -> "other" and max distinct variants per process.

Rafael Mendes (review): From oncall perspective: can we add a quick series-count guardrail? At least a debug metric like `redwood_metrics_label_overflow_total{label="route_group"}` so we can tell if we’re collapsing too much.

Thomas Baird (author): Added `redwood_metrics_label_overflow_total` with `label` and `component` only (bounded). Also added a panel note in the minimum-pack wireframe doc (separate PR) to surface this for troubleshooting.
Logan Wright (review): The helper uses a RWMutex on the hot path. Did you measure impact at 20k rps? Prefer atomic + sync.Map or precomputed mapping if possible.

Thomas Baird (author): Added a micro-benchmark: contention is negligible because we only lock when a new label value appears; steady-state is read-only map access. Also moved the map to a lock-free fast-path after warmup using atomic pointer swap (see bounded_labels.go).
Ethan Park (review): Control plane metrics label names: please align `component` values with the service naming standard (policy-engine vs routing).
Thomas Baird (author): Updated to `component="policy-engine"` and `service="routing"` consistent with standards; also added a small migration note to avoid breaking selectors.
Sergio Costa (comment): FYI dashboards PRs will need to be updated to use `route_group` and `status_class`. Thanks for keeping the compat rules.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved after tenant label changes + overflow metric.
Nadia Rahman (approval): Approved; please ensure we track deprecation removal in a follow-up issue.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved; this should help a lot with customer TSDB blowups.
Thomas Baird (author): Filed follow-up: remove legacy labels after 2 releases + update alert queries once minimum pack GA is cut.
related_incidents_or_tickets: Motivated by noisy alerts/TSDB pressure reported in SUP-49238; aligns with Private minimum pack workstream ENG-19143.
